summary: Grace-period misalignment causes repeated 429s during gRPC reconnect + short-lived key rotation
description:
Issue summary: GlyphSearch reports repeated 429 throttling spikes for low sustained QPS after rolling out a client change that issues short-lived API keys and uses gRPC bidirectional streaming through a shared proxy/load-balancer. Impact: Customer-facing search latency and failed requests for a subset (~8%) of users. They see 429s even though aggregated token usage is well below configured tenant quota.

Observed pattern: 429s appear shortly after client-side key rotation events that coincide with gRPC reconnects. Failures are bursty (10-30s) and correlate with connection churn from mobile clients behind NATs.

Why this is high-priority: A dedicated customer with production traffic is seeing user-visible errors. Root cause not yet confirmed; preliminary evidence points to rate-accounting edge-case when a connection reconnect occurs in the same refill window as a key rotation and proxy-level multiplexing.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a dedicated tenant with per-tenant token quota set to a conservative rate (example: 1200 tokens/min).
2) Use a mobile client that maintains a long-lived gRPC bidi stream to /v1/stream and rotates short-lived API keys every 60s via a backend token service.
3) Put clients behind a shared NAT / proxy that reuses HTTP/2 connections for multiple clients (multiplexing).
4) Trigger a key rotation while forcing a gRPC reconnect (network hiccup / slight keepalive drop).
5) Observe 429 responses on reconnecting sessions for ~10-30s even though overall token consumption is below tenant quota.
logs: 2026-03-10T14:03:22Z | rate-limiter | tenant=glyphsearch | action=consume | tokens=1 | key=short-abc123 | conn_id=lb-78 | status=accepted
2026-03-10T14:04:06Z | rate-limiter | tenant=glyphsearch | action=consume | tokens=1 | key=short-def456 | conn_id=lb-78 | status=throttled | reason=token-window-exhausted
2026-03-10T14:04:13Z | rate-limiter | tenant=glyphsearch | action=consume | tokens=1 | key=short-def456 | status=throttled
investigation_notes: Support/Eng review: confirmed 429s are coming from rate-limiter layer (not upstream model).

Hypothesis: when key rotation + gRPC reconnect occur on pooled/hydra connections, the rate-accounting path can apply leftover consumption to the newly issued short key without applying an inter-key grace, causing immediate token-window exhaustion for that key and resulting in several seconds of 429s until refill syncs.
Evidence: correlation between conn_id reuse in gateway logs and immediate throttle events for the freshly minted key. Throttle counts spike for reconnects using the same connection id.
Checked related telemetry: token_refill_histogram shows a small number of refill windows where accounting does not reset for new key bindings on pooled connections.
Reproduced internally with a test harness that simulates connection reuse + 60s TTL key rotation; observed identical 429 spike pattern.
comments: Diego Ramos (Support): Customer first reported at 2026-03-10 14:08 UTC. Provided trace IDs and sample request ids. Asked for immediate mitigation options.

Maya Patel (SRE): I've collected raw rate-limiter logs and replicates. Adding network-proxy and auth teams to CC. Tentative workaround: avoid rotating keys exactly at the same instant as reconnect events; increase client-side key TTL to widen the overlap window.

Alex Chen (Auth): We see that our token bind operation marks a key->connection mapping but doesn't emit a transient grace token for connection-bound accounting. We'll prototype a transient grace of N=2 tokens on key swap for pooled connections.
Customer reply (GlyphSearch): We can temporarily move to 300s TTL for short keys and throttle rotation frequency. They requested ETA for permanent fix and asked whether console changes are required.
resolution_notes: Workaround (recommended to customer): Increase short-lived key TTL from 60s -> 300s and update client to reuse connections when possible. This immediately reduced 429 spikes for GlyphSearch during their rollout tests.

Short-term engineering mitigation: Auth team to add a 2-token transient grace for newly issued keys if a connection reuse / multiplex event is detected (PR#1423). This is low-risk and scheduled to deploy to staging 2026-03-16.

Long-term fix: Rate-limiter will be updated to associate consumption atomically with (connection_id, key_id) and to clear prior-key residual accounting on key swap. Design doc and rollout plan on Confluence link above.

Follow-ups: Add telemetry for 'key-swap-throttle' meter on the rate-limiter, update SDK guidance to recommend >120s TTL for short-lived keys behind multiplexing proxies, and document known interactions in the Dedicated onboarding guide.
notes_for_follow_up: Track staging rollout for PR#1423 and validate with GlyphSearch test harness before prod rollout.
Add an internal postmortem if customer experiences another production incident after patch deploy.
